question: My battery label just says 22.2V with no cell count. How many LiPo cells in series is that?
reference_answer: A 22.2 V LiPo (or Li-ion) battery is a 6S pack, i.e. six cells in series at 3.7 V nominal each.

question: When flying on a Li-ion pack, what is the realistic minimum per-cell voltage under load, and how does that compare with a LiPo?
reference_answer: The "real" minimum per-cell voltage under load is 2.7 V for Li-ion versus 3.5 V for LiPo. Damage occurs around 2.5 V (Li-ion) and 3.0 V (LiPo) under load.
evidence: | "Real" minimum (voltage under load/while flying) | 3.5 | 2.7 |

question: If a failsafe commands a landing on my VTOL while it is cruising as a plane, what does the vehicle do first?
reference_answer: With the Land mode failsafe action, a VTOL will first transition to multicopter (MC) mode and then land.
evidence: | Land mode | The vehicle will enter Land mode (MC) or Land mode (FW), and land. A VTOL will first transition to MC mode. |

question: Is there a way to force the drone to head home after a fixed number of seconds in the air, and is that on out of the box?
reference_answer: Yes: COM_FLT_TIME_MAX sets the maximum allowed flight time in seconds before Return mode is engaged. It defaults to -1, meaning disabled.
evidence: | Maximum flight time failsafe level | COM_FLT_TIME_MAX | Maximum allowed flight time before Return mode will be engaged, in seconds. `-1`: Disabled (default). |

question: Which parameter decides what the drone does when the RC transmitter link drops out, and what choices does it offer?
reference_answer: NAV_RCL_ACT sets the manual control loss failsafe action. Options are Disabled, Loiter, Return, Land, Disarm, and Terminate.
evidence: | NAV_RCL_ACT | Failsafe Action | Disabled, Loiter, Return, Land, Disarm, Terminate. |

question: I want losing the ground-station telemetry link to be ignored in certain flight modes. What parameter does that, and can I set it from the QGC safety page?
reference_answer: COM_DLL_EXCEPT sets the modes where data link loss will not trigger a failsafe. It is not displayed in the QGC UI, so it must be set as a parameter.
evidence: The following settings also apply, but are not displayed in the QGC UI. ... | Mode exceptions for DLL failsafe | COM_DLL_EXCEPT | Set modes where DL loss will not trigger a failsafe. |

question: What happens to the simple cylinder fence if I leave its maximum horizontal radius at zero?
reference_answer: The horizontal radius is set by GF_MAX_HOR_DIST; if it is 0 the geofence is disabled.
evidence: | Max Radius | GF_MAX_HOR_DIST | Horizontal radius of geofence cylinder. Geofence disabled if 0. |

question: Which parameter sets the horizontal position-error threshold that trips the GNSS-loss failsafe on a hovering vehicle, and how does it apply to fixed-wing planes?
reference_answer: COM_POS_FS_EPH is the horizontal position error threshold for hovering vehicles (multicopters and VTOLs in hover). Fixed-wing vehicles have this value set to infinity.
evidence: | COM_POS_FS_EPH | Horizontal position error threshold for hovering vehicles (Multicopters and VTOLs in hover). Fixed-wing vehicles have this value set to infinity. |

question: On a plane that loses GPS, what controls how long it circles waiting for the fix to come back, and how do I turn that waiting off?
reference_answer: FW_GPSF_LT is the loiter time spent waiting for GPS recovery before going into land or flight termination; set it to 0 to disable. FW_GPSF_R sets the fixed bank angle while circling.
evidence: | FW_GPSF_LT | Loiter time (waiting for GPS recovery before it goes into land or flight termination). Set to 0 to disable. |

question: During the front transition, what limits how much height a VTOL can lose before it gives up and reverts to multicopter mode?
reference_answer: VT_QC_T_ALT_LOSS: the quad-chute is triggered if the vehicle falls this far below its initial altitude before completing the transition to fixed-wing flight.
evidence: | VT_QC_T_ALT_LOSS | Altitude loss threshold for quad-chute triggering during VTOL transition to fixed-wing flight.

question: By default does PX4 do anything when the wind exceeds the maximum threshold? What value would make it return home instead?
reference_answer: COM_WIND_MAX_ACT defaults to 0 (None), so no action is taken by default. Setting it to 3 selects Return.
evidence: `0`: None (Default), `1`: Warning, `2`: Hold, `3`: Return, `4`: Terminate, `5`: Land.

question: How long does the vehicle's pitch have to stay past the limit before the failure detector flags it?
reference_answer: FD_FAIL_P_TTRI sets the time the pitch must exceed FD_FAIL_P for failure detection; the default is 0.3 s.
evidence: | FD_FAIL_P_TTRI | Time to exceed FD_FAIL_P for failure detection (default 0.3s). |

question: Can PX4 drop a motor it thinks has died out of the mix and keep flying on the remaining ones?
reference_answer: Yes. CA_FAILURE_MODE can be configured to remove the first motor that detects a failure from the allocation effectiveness, turning it off and operating the vehicle without it until the next disarm.
evidence: | CA_FAILURE_MODE | Configure to not only warn about a motor failure but remove the first motor that detects a failure from the allocation effectiveness

question: What PWM threshold does an external automatic parachute trigger need to send before PX4 engages the failsafe?
reference_answer: FD_EXT_ATS_TRIG sets the PWM threshold from the external automatic trigger system; the default is 1900 (listed as 1900 ms). The input itself is enabled with FD_EXT_ATS_EN.
evidence: | FD_EXT_ATS_TRIG | The PWM threshold from external automatic trigger system for engaging failsafe. Default: 1900 ms. |

question: Out of the box, will PX4 let me arm with no GPS, and which parameter controls that?
reference_answer: Yes. COM_ARM_WO_GPS enables arming without GPS and is 1 (Enabled) by default.
evidence: | COM_ARM_WO_GPS | Enable arming without GPS. `0`: Disabled, `1`: Enabled (default). |

question: Walk me through calibrating the accelerometer in QGroundControl.
reference_answer: Connect the vehicle in QGC, open Vehicle Setup > Sensors, click Accelerometer and press OK. Place the vehicle in each orientation shown, holding it still when the image turns yellow until it turns green, and repeat for all orientations until 'Calibration complete' is displayed.
evidence: Position the vehicle as guided by the _images_ on the screen. Once prompted (the orientation-image turns yellow) hold the vehicle still.

question: How do I use QGC's semi-automatic tool to map my quad's motors to the PWM outputs?
reference_answer: With props removed: set up the motor geometry, select the PWM tab, click Identify & Assign Motors, then for each motor that spins select the corresponding motor in the geometry section (use Spin Motor Again if needed). After all motors are assigned the tool sets the mapping and exits.
evidence: 1. Click the **Identify & Assign Motors** button. 1. One motor will start spinning (click **Spin Motor Again** if it stops spinning too quickly to note.)

question: What's the step-by-step process for dialing in each motor's disarmed, minimum and maximum PWM values with the test sliders?
reference_answer: For each motor (props off): snap the slider to the bottom and lower the disarmed value until the motor doesn't spin; move up to the minimum position and adjust minimum so the motor barely spins; raise the slider to check spin direction/positive thrust; then at maximum, reduce the maximum value in small 25us steps while listening, using the value where the tone last changes.
evidence: Reduce the value of the PWM output's `maximum` value just below the default. Listen to the tone of the motors as you increase the value in small (25us) increments.

question: How should I set the PWM limits for a flap servo that only deflects one way from retracted?
reference_answer: Set PWM CENT params to -1, then Disarmed 1500, Min 1200, Max 1700. Check the slider extends the flap (else Rev Range), adjust Disarmed until the flap is flush and set Min or Max to match it, then set the other limit so the flap is fully extended at the top of the slider. For PWM servos set Center midway between Min and Max.

heading_path: Control surfaces that move from neutral to full deflection

evidence: 1. Set values `Disarmed` to `1500`, `Min` to `1200`, `Max` to `1700` so that the values are around the centre of the servo range.

question: How do I bench-check the servos that tilt the motors on my tiltrotor after setting the frame rate?
reference_answer: For each tilt servo: set the Disarmed value (e.g. 1000 or 2000 for PWM) so it points the expected way when disarmed; put the slider at its lowest position and verify it points toward Angle at Min Tilt; then put it at the highest position and verify thrust points toward Angle at Max Tilt.
evidence: Position the slider for the servo in the lowest position, and verify that a positive value increase will point towards the `Angle at Min Tilt`

question: After flashing PX4, how do I pick my airframe in QGroundControl?
reference_answer: Connect the vehicle, open Vehicle Setup > Airframe, choose the broad vehicle group and then the specific airframe from its dropdown, and click Apply and Restart, then Apply in the prompt to save and reboot.
evidence: 1. Click **Apply and Restart**. Click **Apply** in the following prompt to save the settings and restart the vehicle.

question: What are the steps to calibrate the pitot/airspeed sensor?
reference_answer: Connect in QGC, make sure the airspeed sensor driver is enabled, open Vehicle Setup > Sensors and click Airspeed. Shield the sensor from wind (cup it without blocking holes), click OK, then blow into the pitot tip when asked; QGC reports success or failure.
evidence: Shield the sensor from the wind (i.e. cup it with your hand). Take care not to block any of its holes.

question: Before autotuning a plane, how do I check it's stable enough to go ahead?
reference_answer: Do a preflight check, take off and fly at cruise speed in Position or Altitude mode, then roll left > right > center over about 3 s, confirming it settles within 2 oscillations; increase amplitude up to ~20 degrees, then repeat on the pitch axis.
evidence: 2. Take off and fly at cruise speed in Position mode or Altitude mode.

question: How do I set up a transmitter switch to start and stop fixed-wing autotuning?
reference_answer: Pick an RC channel for the switch, set RC_MAP_AUX1 (or any RC_MAP_AUX1-6) to that channel, then set FW_AT_MAN_AUX to the matching aux (e.g. 1: Aux 1). The tuner is enabled above 0.5 and disabled below 0.5.
evidence: 3. Set FW_AT_MAN_AUX to the selected channel (i.e. `1: Aux 1` if you mapped `RC_MAP_AUX1`).

question: My vehicle is too big to rotate for a compass calibration. What do I do instead?
reference_answer: Use the large vehicle calibration: get a GNSS fix, align the vehicle to face True North as accurately as possible, then in the QGC MAVLink Console run `commander calibrate mag quick` (or send MAV_CMD_FIXED_MAG_CAL_YAW).
evidence: 2. Align the vehicle to face True North. ... commander calibrate mag quick

question: How do I flash the current stable PX4 release onto a Pixhawk using QGC?
reference_answer: With USB and battery disconnected, start QGC and open Vehicle Setup > Firmware, connect the flight controller directly to a powered USB port (not a hub), select PX4 Pro Stable Release, and click OK; the board reboots and reconnects when done.
evidence: 1. Select the **PX4 Pro Stable Release vX.x.x** option to install the latest stable version of PX4 _for your flight controller_ (autodetected).

question: What's the sequence for calibrating my RC transmitter sticks in QGroundControl?
reference_answer: Turn on the transmitter, connect the vehicle, open Vehicle Setup > Radio and press OK. Choose the transmitter mode, move the sticks to each indicated position pressing Next, move all other switches/dials through their full range, then press Next to save.
evidence: 1. When prompted, move all other switches and dials through their full range (you will be able to observe them moving on the _Channel Monitor_).

question: How do I move the trim offsets from my radio's trim knobs into the autopilot?
reference_answer: Select Copy Trims, center the sticks with throttle all the way down, press Ok, and then reset the trims on the transmitter back to zero.
evidence: 1. Center your sticks and move throttle all the way down. 1. Press **Ok**. 1. Reset the trims on your transmitter back to zero.

question: How do I hook a dial on my transmitter up to a PX4 parameter so I can tweak it in flight?
reference_answer: In Radio setup map up to 3 dials/sliders to channels and assign them to PARAM Tuning Ids. Then in Parameters select the parameter, tick Advanced Settings, click Set RC to Param..., choose the tuning channel (1, 2 or 3), press OK and then Save.
evidence: 1. Click the **Set RC to Param...** button (this will pop-up the foreground dialog displayed below)

question: How do I turn on the battery estimation mode that combines voltage with integrated current?
reference_answer: First set up voltage estimation with load compensation (including calibrating the amps-per-volt divider), then set BAT1_CAPACITY to around 90% of the battery's advertised capacity, not higher.

heading_path: Voltage-based Estimation Fused with Current Integration

evidence: 2. Set the parameter BAT1_CAPACITY to around 90% of the advertised battery capacity (usually printed on the battery label).

question: What does "toilet bowling" mean, and what is it a symptom of?
reference_answer: Toilet bowling is a multicopter circling at increasing radius (spiraling out, usually at constant altitude, leading to fly-away); it indicates a poor compass calibration.
evidence: toilet bowling (circling at increasing radius/spiraling-out, usually constant altitude, leading to fly-way)

question: Where in the PX4 source tree is the list of actuator output functions defined?
reference_answer: The output functions are defined in /src/lib/mixer_module/output_functions.yaml (the documented list is correct as of PX4 v1.15).
evidence: The functions are defined in source at /src/lib/mixer_module/output_functions.yaml.

question: When entering motor X/Y/Z positions, what are they measured relative to? Is it the flight controller?
reference_answer: Positions are in the FRD body frame (X forward, Y right, Z down) with the origin at the vehicle's centre of gravity, which may not be where the flight controller is.
evidence: The origin is the vehicle's **centre-of-gravity (COG)**. This may **NOT** be the same position as the location of the autopilot.

question: My rover's drive motor needs to spin both ways. What do I tick in the motor geometry, and what does the ESC need?
reference_answer: Select the Reversible checkbox (an advanced option) for that motor, and make sure the ESC is configured for it, e.g. 3D mode enabled for DShot ESCs.
evidence: make sure to select the **Reversible** checkbox for those motors ... 3D mode enabled for DShot ESCs

question: If I raise the roll scale value on an elevon, do the surfaces move more or less?
reference_answer: Less. The scale values go into the allocation matrix, which is inverted, so increasing the scale reduces the control surface deflection.

heading_path: Actuator Roll, Pitch, and Yaw Scaling

evidence: Increasing the scale will _reduce_ the deflection of the control surfaces (as it gets inverted).

question: Which parameter can I use to lock out actuator testing completely?
reference_answer: COM_MOT_TEST_EN can be used to completely disable actuator testing.
evidence: The parameter COM_MOT_TEST_EN can be used to completely disable actuator testing.

question: What logging settings capture raw comparison data for all the magnetometers?
reference_answer: Set SDLOG_MODE=1 and SDLOG_PROFILE=64 to log raw comparison data for magnetometers (and all sensors).
evidence: can be logged by setting SDLOG_MODE=1 and SDLOG_PROFILE=64.

question: When working out board rotation offsets, what does "extrinsic rotation" refer to?
reference_answer: It means the axes being rotated around (forward x, right y, down z) stay fixed from one rotation step to the next, so the frame the rotation is performed in does not move.
evidence: The axes to rotate around stay the same from one rotation step to the next one. So the frame to perform the rotation in stays fixed. This is also known as _extrinsic rotation_.

question: What value do I give COM_RC_IN_MODE to fly with a gamepad?
reference_answer: Set COM_RC_IN_MODE=1 (Joystick); values 2 or 3 also enable joystick under some circumstances.
evidence: Set the parameter COM_RC_IN_MODE=1 - `Joystick`

question: Autotune on my heavy-lift octocopter isn't working well. Which parameter is suggested for big vehicles?
reference_answer: For big multicopters you may need to increase MC_AT_RISE_TIME, the desired rise time of the step response, which takes some trial and error.
evidence: For big multicopter vehicles you may need to increase the desired raise time of the step response MC_AT_RISE_TIME.

question: What internal resistance per cell is typical for a LiPo, if I want to set it by hand?
reference_answer: A typical value is about 5mΩ per cell (it varies with discharge rating, age and health); it can be set manually in BAT1_R_INTERNAL.
evidence: A typical value for LiPo batteries is 5mΩ per cell but this can vary with discharge current rating, age and health of the cells.

question: Which industry standard calls for an external automatic trigger system for the failure detector?
reference_answer: External ATS is required by ASTM F3322-18 (an example device is the FruityChutes SATS-MINI).
evidence: External ATS is required by ASTM F3322-18.

question: In which flight modes is the failure detector inactive?
reference_answer: It is inactive where the vehicle is expected to flip: Acro mode (MC), Acro mode (FW), and Manual (FW).
evidence: except for those where the vehicle is _expected_ to do flips (i.e. Acro mode (MC), Acro mode (FW), and Manual (FW)).

question: Where is the check that stops a mission starting when its first waypoint is too far away documented?
reference_answer: Mission feasibility checks are not failsafes, so they are documented in Mission Mode (FW) > Mission Feasibility Checks and Mission Mode (MC) > Mission Feasibility Checks.
evidence: As these are not strictly speaking "failsafes" they are documented in Mission Mode (FW) > Mission Feasibility Checks and Mission Mode (MC) > Mission Feasibility Checks.

question: I have a TE MS4525 airspeed sensor that isn't showing up. Which parameter starts its driver?
reference_answer: Airspeed drivers are not started automatically; the TE MS4525 is enabled with SENS_EN_MS4525DO.
evidence: TE MS4525 (SENS_EN_MS4525DO)

question: How do fixed-wing and multicopter autotuning differ in when the new gains are applied by default, and which parameter controls each?
reference_answer: Fixed-wing uses FW_AT_APPLY, defaulting to 2 (apply immediately in air, then monitor stability for 4 s and revert if unstable). Multicopter uses MC_AT_APPLY, defaulting to 1 (apply after disarm, then test with a careful takeoff).
evidence: This behaviour can be configured using the FW_AT_APPLY parameter: ... This behaviour can be configured using the MC_AT_APPLY parameter:

question: During the pre-autotune stability check I get slow oscillations, about one per second. What do I adjust on a plane versus on a multicopter?
reference_answer: On a fixed-wing, increase FW_R_TC and FW_P_TC in steps of 0.1. On a multicopter, decrease MC_ROLL_P and MC_PITCH_P in steps of 1.0. In both cases the attitude loop is too fast relative to the rate loop.

heading_path: Drone oscillates when performing the pre-tuning test
Drone oscillates when performing the pre-tuning test

evidence: Increase FW_R_TC and FW_P_TC by steps of 0.1. ... Decrease MC_ROLL_P and MC_PITCH_P by steps of 1.0.

question: What's the practical difference between the kill switch and the kill gesture if I trigger one by accident, and what parameter governs each?
reference_answer: A kill switch can be reverted: motors restart if the switch is reverted within COM_KILL_DISARM (default 5 s), after which the vehicle disarms. A kill gesture cannot be reverted without a reboot; its hold time is MAN_KILL_GEST_T, default -1 (disabled).
evidence: | COM_KILL_DISARM | Timeout value for disarming after kill switch is engaged. Default: `5` seconds. | ... The action cannot be reverted without a reboot

question: My receiver just keeps outputting the last good signal when the transmitter is off. Will PX4 notice, how do I fix it, and which parameter then picks the failsafe action?
reference_answer: No, PX4 cannot detect a receiver that repeats the last signal. Configure the receiver to output a low throttle value on loss and set that value in RC_FAILS_THR. The action on manual control loss is set by NAV_RCL_ACT.
evidence: Output the last received signal (_cannot be detected by PX4_ as it looks like valid input). ... | NAV_RCL_ACT | Failsafe Action |

question: For the current-integration battery estimate, what should BAT1_CAPACITY be set to, and which parameter holds the amps-per-volt calibration that must be done first?
reference_answer: Set BAT1_CAPACITY to around 90% of the advertised battery capacity. The amps-per-volt divider, which must be calibrated beforehand, is stored in BAT1_A_PER_V (BAT2_A_PER_V for battery 2).

heading_path: Voltage-based Estimation Fused with Current Integration

evidence: Set the parameter BAT1_CAPACITY to around 90% of the advertised battery capacity ... This setting corresponds to parameter(s): BAT1_A_PER_V and BAT2_A_PER_V.

question: For a LiPo pack, what per-cell 'full' voltage is recommended, and what is the conservative no-load 'empty' level?
reference_answer: Full voltage per cell should be 4.05 V (the QGC default for LiPo). The conservative minimum (no-load) per-cell voltage for LiPo is 3.7 V, with 3.5 V as the real minimum under load.
evidence: **LiPo:** 4.05V (default in _QGroundControl_) ... | Conservative (voltage under no-load) | 3.7 | 3 |

question: I want a mid-air flip to trigger flight termination (to fire a parachute). What do I have to enable, and which parameters set the roll and pitch limits?
reference_answer: In-flight action on detected failures is off by default; enable it by setting CBRK_FLIGHTTERM=0 (unset from the default 121212). The attitude trigger limits are FD_FAIL_R (max roll) and FD_FAIL_P (max pitch), in degrees.
evidence: Acting on a detected failure during flight is deactivated by default (enable by setting the parameter: CBRK_FLIGHTTERM=0). ... | FD_FAIL_R | Maximum allowed roll (in degrees). |

question: RC loss is set to Return and ground-station link loss is set to Land. If both links drop, which action wins, and which parameter controls how long the telemetry link must be gone before its failsafe fires?
reference_answer: When multiple failsafes trigger, the more severe action is taken, so Land is executed. The data link loss timeout is COM_DL_LOSS_T.
evidence: If multiple failsafes are triggered, the more severe action is taken. ... | Data Link Loss Timeout | COM_DL_LOSS_T |

question: By default, will PX4 refuse to arm on a low battery, and what does it do by default when it estimates there's only just enough charge left to get home?
reference_answer: No: COM_ARM_BAT_MIN (minimum battery for arming) defaults to 0, disabled. The low-flight-time-for-safe-return action COM_FLTT_LOW_ACT defaults to 3, Return mode.
evidence: | COM_ARM_BAT_MIN | Minimum battery level for arming. `0`: Disabled (default). ... `3`: Return mode (default). |

question: Using a FrSky Taranis, how do I get its SD 3-position switch to change flight modes, and what do I then do in QGroundControl?
reference_answer: On the Taranis MIXER page edit CH5 and set its Source to the SD switch, so channel 5 outputs three PWM values. In QGC open Vehicle Setup > Flight Modes, select channel 5 as the Mode channel, and choose a flight mode for each switch position (slot).

heading_path: Taranis Setup: 3-way Switch Configuration for Single-Channel Mode

evidence: Press **ENT(ER)** to edit the **CH5** configuration then change the **Source** to be the *SD* button. ... Select the **Mode channel**

question: My tiltrotor's servos swing from straight up to straight forward. What min/max tilt angles do I enter in the geometry, and how do I then verify direction with the test sliders?
reference_answer: A servo moving between upright and forward uses Angle at min tilt = 0 and Angle at max tilt = 90. Then set the Disarmed value, and check that at the lowest slider position the servo points toward Angle at Min Tilt and at the highest position thrust points toward Angle at Max Tilt.
evidence: between the upright and forward positions would have `min=0` and `max=90`. ... Position the slider for the servo in the lowest position

question: Which compass calibration is meant for a quick routine check before a flight, what does it compensate for, and when does its result actually get saved?
reference_answer: The Partial (quick) calibration is the routine pre-flight option; it only estimates offsets for hard iron effects. It applies immediately but is saved to parameters only after the vehicle is disarmed, so it is lost if no arm/disarm happens before shutdown.
evidence: This type of calibration only estimates the offsets to compensate for a hard iron effect. ... is saved to the calibration parameters after disarming the vehicle only

question: After choosing my airframe, when do I need to run ESC calibration, and do DShot ESCs need their command limits set up?
reference_answer: ESC calibration should be done after mapping actuators to outputs if you use PWM or OneShot ESCs. DShot ESCs do not need command-limit configuration, only rotation direction.
evidence: After mapping actuators to outputs you should perform ESC Calibration if using PWM or OneShot ESCs. ... DShot ESCs do not require configuration of the command limits but only rotation direction.

question: How do I tell PX4 which way my flight controller is mounted, and then correct a small leftover tilt so the artificial horizon reads level?
reference_answer: In QGC Vehicle Setup > Sensors click Orientations, select the AutoPilot Orientation and press OK. Then in Sensors click Level Horizon, place the vehicle in its level-flight orientation on a level surface (hover position for copters, level-flight attitude for planes), press OK and wait for it to finish.
evidence: 1. Select the **AutoPilot Orientation** (as calculated above). ... 1. Click the **Level Horizon** button.

question: On a multicopter, what conditions trip the position-loss failsafe, and what flight mode does it fall back to?
reference_answer: It triggers on a timeout since the last velocity/position-aiding sensor data (EKF2_NOAID_TOUT) or when estimated horizontal accuracy exceeds COM_POS_FS_EPH. Multicopters then switch to Altitude mode if a height estimate is available, otherwise Stabilized mode.
evidence: | EKF2_NOAID_TOUT | Maximum inertial dead-reckoning time ... Multicopters will switch to Altitude mode if a height estimate is available, otherwise Stabilized mode.
